Notes on Graphics Devices

man-devices.Rd

The trainer makes extensive use of getGraphicsEvent to capture mouse movements and keyboard inputs. Only some graphics devices support this. If you receive the error message ‘The graphics device does not support event handling’ when starting the trainer, then the default graphics device used does not support this kind of interactivity. For example, this will be the case for the RStudioGD graphics device that is used by RStudio. You can try running windows() (under Windows) or x11() (under macOS or Linux) before starting the trainer with play().

Under Windows, you could also run R with RGui, which uses the windows plotting device by default (this is actually the recommended way to run the trainer under Windows). Under macOS or Linux, you can just run R from the command line.

If the graphics look fuzzy under RGui, then this might be related to high DPI scaling (under high resolutions, it is common to scale apps by 150% or 200% so that text and graphical elements are not tiny; see the display settings under Windows). To avoid this issue, go the the properties of RGui, select Compatibility, Change high DPI settings, High DPI scaling override, and select ‘Application’. After restarting RGui, the graphics should look sharper.

The F10 function key is registered under Windows, but is also the operating system key for activating the menu bar, which is annoying. You can use the Ctrl + 1 keyboard shortcut instead. For some reason, the F11 and F12 function keys are not registered at all. You can use Ctrl + 2 and Ctrl + 3 respectively instead.

Occasionally, the graphics window flickers under Windows, especially when making rapid updates to the graphics being shown. The exact cause of this is unknown.
